_comment: Hand-maintained companion to the cargo-about output.
Everything here is something cargo-about cannot see: C/C++ sources compiled
into the binary by a -sys crate, prebuilt DLLs the Windows installer copies,
fonts and data files under assets/, ML models fetched at runtime, and the
commands/generate_licenses.ps1 merges this with the cargo-about output into
flag: null | "notice" (must be shown / worth knowing) | "caution" (needs
action before commercial distribution). Anything flagged is surfaced in the
'Commercial distribution notes' section of the in-app Licenses window.

topic: entries sharing a topic collapse into one row in the window's summary section, so a single issue spread across a wrapper crate, its -sys crate and the C library it builds is stated once rather than three times.

feature: the cargo feature that gates this component. The window resolves it at runtime with cfg! so the page reports what the binary in front of you actually contains, and obligations for components that are not compiled in are not claimed.

licenses.name: GNU Library General Public License v2.0
Universal Category System terms of use
What you may do with a NeoWaves build

components.name: NeoWaves distribution terms
components.note: NeoWaves's own source is MIT. MP3 export loads a separate, user-replaceable LAME shared library using the LGPL-2.0 section 6(b) mechanism; LAME is not incorporated into the executable. AAC encode/decode support is intentionally absent. Open this entry for the redistribution checklist.

components.name: LAME (libmp3lame)
components.note: MP3 export, behind the `mp3_lame` feature. Built from the unmodified LAME 3.100 source under vendor/lame-3.100 and shipped as libmp3lame.dll beside NeoWaves. The executable imports the DLL and users may replace it with an ABI-compatible build, using LGPL-2.0 section 6(b)'s shared-library mechanism. The LAME acknowledgement, project link, copyright and full LGPL-2.0 text are shipped in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt and shown in Help > Licenses. The exact corresponding LAME source is in the public NeoWaves source tree. The software licence does not itself grant patent rights; distributors must assess other rights in their jurisdictions.

components.name: Cisco OpenH264
components.note: NOT IN THE DEFAULT BUILD. Cisco pays the AVC/H.264 patent pool only for users of Cisco's own prebuilt binaries; compiling the bundled C++ sources, as this crate does, moves that obligation to whoever ships the result. So `video` was taken out of the default feature set. The only binary this project releases is the Windows installer, where open_video_decoder tries Media Foundation first anyway (H.264, HEVC, VP9, hardware accelerated), so nothing was lost. If you build with --features video and then redistribute that binary, the AVC obligation is yours.

components.name: SQLite
components.authors: D. Richard Hipp and the SQLite authors
components.note: Amalgamation compiled in through the rusqlite `bundled` feature. Public domain; no obligations.

components.name: Signalsmith Stretch (C++)
components.note: The pitch-shift / time-stretch engine, compiled from the git submodule under vendor/. The Rust wrapper crate (Colin Marc) is MIT as well and is listed separately with the crates.

components.name: ONNX Runtime
components.version: statically linked via the ort crate
components.note: Machine-learning inference for the transcription and music-analysis features. The `ort` crate's download-binaries feature fetches a static library and links it into the executable -- there is no onnxruntime DLL to ship. Static linking does not remove the attribution requirement; MIT still wants the notice below to travel with the binary.

components.name: DirectML execution provider
components.note: NOT REDISTRIBUTED. On Windows the ONNX Runtime DirectML execution provider is asked for first and falls back to CPU silently if it is unavailable (music_onnx.rs). DirectML.dll itself is a Windows component that has shipped with the OS since Windows 10 1903; NeoWaves calls it rather than bundling it, so no redistribution terms attach. Listed here only so the dependency is visible.

components.name: Oniguruma
components.note: Regex engine behind the tokenizers crate's `onig` feature, used by the transcription model's tokenizer. onig-sys compiles the C sources with `cc`, so it is statically linked on every platform and its BSD-2 notice ships inside the executable.

components.name: Noto Sans JP
components.note: Embedded as assets/fonts/NotoSansJP-Regular.otf for Japanese UI text. SIL OFL 1.1: the font may ship with the application, but the licence must travel with it and the font itself may not be sold on its own.

components.name: Universal Category System 8.2.1 category data
components.note: Embedded as src/metadata/data/ucs_8_2_1.tsv for offline CatID lookup. Published as a public-domain initiative, free for commercial use.

components.name: Zoo default assets
components.note: assets/zoo/default.gif and assets/zoo/default.wav, embedded in the binary by src/app/zoo_assets.rs. Made by the author of NeoWaves and covered by the same MIT licence as the rest of the project.

components.name: Steinberg VST 3 interface
components.note: RESOLVED as of VST 3.8 (2025-10-29): Steinberg relicensed the VST 3 SDK to MIT, replacing the old GPLv3-or-proprietary dual licence. No agreement to sign and no GPL to take on. NeoWaves redistributes no Steinberg source in any case -- the `vst3` crate ships its own MIT/Apache-2.0 bindings. What remains is the trademark: VST is a registered trademark of Steinberg Media Technologies GmbH. NeoWaves does not use ASIO, which moved to GPLv3/proprietary terms.

components.name: onnx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo
components.note: Downloaded at runtime for transcription; not redistributed with NeoWaves. Pinned to the revision shown above. The upstream openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo weights are MIT, but the ONNX conversion repository carries no licence tag of its own; obtain explicit confirmation before redistributing those converted files.

components.name: deepghs/silero-vad-onnx
components.note: Voice activity detection for transcription segmentation. Downloaded at runtime; not redistributed.

components.name: zukky/allinone-DLL-ONNX
components.authors: Taejun Kim (All-In-One Music Structure Analyzer), Meta AI (Demucs v4)
components.note: Beat/downbeat/section models (harmonix-*) from mir-aidj/all-in-one and stem separation (htdemucs) from facebookresearch/demucs, both MIT upstream. Downloaded at runtime; not redistributed. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md in that repository.

epaint_default_fonts.note: Carries egui's bundled default fonts (Hack, Ubuntu-Light, Noto Emoji), which is why OFL-1.1 and Ubuntu-font-1.0 appear in an otherwise font-free dependency graph. Both permit redistribution inside an application; their texts must ship with it.

openh264.note: BSD-2-Clause, but openh264-sys2 compiles Cisco's C++ rather than using Cisco's prebuilt binary, which is what moves the AVC patent obligation to the distributor. Off by default now -- see the Cisco OpenH264 entry under Bundled native code.

openh264-sys2.note: Compiles Cisco's OpenH264 from bundled C++ sources. See the Cisco OpenH264 entry under Bundled native code.

option-ext.note: MPL-2.0, file-level copyleft, pulled in transitively by the directory-lookup crates. Same shape as Symphonia: unmodified use imposes only the notice requirement.

symphonia*.note: MPL-2.0, file-level copyleft. Fine to ship in a commercial product — it does not reach the rest of the binary — but any modified Symphonia source file must be published, and the MPL notice must accompany the distribution. Every symphonia-* subcrate carries the same terms.

vst3.note: MIT/Apache-2.0 bindings that ship no Steinberg source. Since VST 3.8 the SDK they describe is itself MIT, so nothing here is copyleft; only the VST trademark still applies.

webpki-root-certs.note: Embeds the Mozilla CA root store as data under CDLA-Permissive-2.0. Permissive and commercially usable; the attribution must be preserved.

webpki-roots.note: Embeds the Mozilla CA root store as data under CDLA-Permissive-2.0. Permissive and commercially usable; the attribution must be preserved.
